theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why should you ask a client about her job before designing her nail art?
options: So that you can charge her a higher price for the art
So that you can tell her friends where she works
Some jobs, such as food handling, limit nail length and art
So that you can choose her favourite colour for her

questions.stem: What is the best way to help a client choose a nail art design?
options: Show her a portfolio or sample tips and discuss her ideas
Choose the design you like best yourself and start straight away
Copy the design that the last client chose that day
Ask her to draw the full design herself on paper

questions.stem: Which condition stops a nail art service on the affected nail and needs a referral?
options: Small white spots on the nail plate
Ridges that run along the length of the nail
Nails that are short and slightly bitten
A thick, yellow nail with a fungal infection

questions.stem: A client has red, swollen, painful skin around one nail. What is this likely to be, and what should you do?
options: A hangnail: cut the swollen skin away with cuticle nippers
An infection: do not treat it and refer her to a doctor
A bruise: paint a darker colour over it
Dry skin: rub cuticle oil in hard

questions.stem: What should be done with an orange stick after it has been used on a client?
options: Wash it and put it back in the drawer
Throw it away, because it is single-use
Soak it in polish remover and use it again
Keep it for the same client's next visit

questions.stem: How should metal tools, such as a dotting tool, be made ready for the next client?
options: Wipe off the polish with a tissue and then use it straight away
Leave it in the UV cabinet for a few seconds
Clean off the product, then disinfect it as the maker says
Rinse it in cold water and dry it on your apron

questions.stem: Why are the nail plates wiped with a nail cleanser (dehydrator) before the base coat?
options: To remove oil and dust so the polish sticks well
To make the nails grow faster under the polish
To soften the cuticles so that they can be cut away
To add colour to the nails before the base coat

questions.stem: What is the main job of a base coat?
options: To add glitter and sparkle to the finished design
To dry the colour coat in a few seconds
To remove old polish from the nail plate
To protect the nail and help the colour stick

questions.stem: Why is a top coat applied over the finished nail art?
options: To seal and protect the design and add shine
To wipe away any small mistakes from the design
To soften the nail so it can be shaped
To make the colours look lighter

questions.stem: Why should the top coat be 'capped' over the free edge (the tip) of the nail?
options: To make the nail look longer than it is
To stop the client from biting the nail
To seal the tip and help stop chipping
To make the polish dry more slowly

questions.stem: Which tool is best for making neat round dots in a design?
options: A fan brush
A dotting tool
A striping brush
A nail file

questions.stem: Which brush is used to paint long, fine, straight lines?
options: A wide fan brush
A flat shader brush
A round powder brush
A long striper brush

questions.stem: What effect is a fan brush often used to create?
options: Tiny dots placed in a straight line
A solid, flat colour with no streaks showing
Soft streaks or a blended, feathered look
A sharp French smile line

questions.stem: How is an ombre (gradient) effect usually made on the nail?
options: By dabbing two or more colours on with a small sponge
By painting one colour very thickly over the whole nail
By cutting a sticker into thin strips
By pressing a stamping plate onto bare nails

questions.stem: In a French manicure, what is the curved edge of the white tip called?
options: The cuticle line
The smile line
The lunula line
The side wall line

questions.stem: What is needed to transfer a design by the stamping method?
options: A fan brush, water and a towel
Striping tape, glitter and a small sponge
Gems, glue and an orange stick
An etched plate, a scraper and a stamper

questions.stem: How should a rhinestone (small gem) be picked up and placed on the nail?
options: With your fingertips, pressing it in hard
With the tip of the polish bottle brush
By dropping it from a height onto the nail
With a wax pencil or a dotting tool

questions.stem: Why must gems be set in top coat, gel or nail adhesive and then sealed?
options: So they stay in place and do not catch or fall off
So that they change colour in the sunlight
So that they can be removed again in a few minutes
So that they make the nail grow stronger

questions.stem: When applying a nail art sticker (decal), what should you do after placing it?
options: Leave it uncovered so the client can peel it later
Soak it in polish remover to make it stick
Press it down flat, then seal it under a layer of top coat
Paint a thick base coat on top of the art

questions.stem: How is a water-slide decal applied?
options: Heated with a hairdryer until it melts onto the nail
Soaked briefly, slid onto the nail, then sealed
Glued with strong glue onto the cuticle
Painted on freehand with a striping brush

questions.stem: What is marbling in nail art?
options: Swirling two or more colours together to look like marble
Painting the whole nail one plain colour with no shine at all
Sticking small stones onto the cuticle
Filing the nail into a round, ball-like shape

questions.stem: What is striping tape used for?
options: To protect the skin around the cuticle from polish
To hold the client's fingers still
To remove old polish from the nail
To make neat, straight lines in a design

questions.stem: When striping tape is used as a guide to mask part of the nail, when is it usually removed?
options: After the top coat is completely hard
While the polish over it is still slightly wet
The next day, after the client has gone home
Before any polish has been put over it

questions.stem: Why must uncured gel polish be kept off the client's skin?
options: It will turn the skin a bright blue colour
It will make the gel dry too quickly
Repeated skin contact can cause an allergy
It will make the lamp stop working

questions.stem: How long should gel polish be cured under the LED or UV lamp?
options: For as long as the client would like
Always exactly ten seconds
For the time the gel maker gives
Until the lamp feels hot

questions.stem: Why must the nail station be well ventilated?
options: To keep the nail polish from drying too fast
To carry away the fumes from polish, remover and gel
To keep the client cool so she does not sweat
To blow dust onto the floor instead of the table

questions.stem: How should nail polish, top coat and remover be stored?
options: On a sunny window sill so they stay runny
Next to the wax heater so they are warm
In the staff fridge with the food and drinks
Tightly closed, in a cool place away from heat and flames

questions.stem: Where should cotton soaked in polish remover be put?
options: In a lidded metal bin, emptied often
In an open box on the nail station
In the client's handbag to take home
On the floor beside the chair

questions.stem: What information does a product's safety data sheet give?
options: The price of the product in each shop in Kingston
Its hazards, safe use, storage and first aid
A list of clients who have used the product
The colours that are in fashion this season

questions.stem: Polish remover splashes into a client's eye. What should you do first?
options: Wipe the eye with a cotton pad soaked in remover
Ask her to keep blinking until it stops stinging
Rinse the eye with plenty of clean cool water
Cover the eye with a dry tissue and carry on

questions.stem: What is an 'accent nail' in a nail art design?
options: One nail decorated differently to catch the eye
The nail that is filed shortest on each hand
A nail with no polish or base coat on it at all
The thumbnail, which always has the most art

questions.stem: A client, Petagaye, wants nails for Independence Day in the colours of the Jamaican flag. Which colours should you use?
options: Red, white and blue
Pink, purple and silver
Red, gold and green
Black, green and gold

questions.stem: Which pair of colours are complementary (opposite each other on the colour wheel)?
options: Blue and green
Red and orange
Yellow and orange
Purple and yellow

questions.stem: Why should a design be balanced across both hands?
options: So that the client pays for the art on both hands
So the polish dries at the same speed
So that the overall look is even and pleasing
So the nails grow at the same rate

questions.stem: Which nail art design is usually best for very short nails?
options: A small, simple design that does not crowd the nail
A large, busy scene with many tiny details and gems on it
Heavy 3D charms built up across the whole nail
A long design that runs past the free edge

questions.stem: Polish has flooded onto the skin around the cuticle. How should it be cleaned off?
options: Leave it there; it will peel off the skin in a day or two
With a fine brush or orange stick dipped in remover
Scrape it off with a metal file
Cover it with more polish

questions.stem: Which sign shows that a nail art design has been finished to a good standard?
options: Thick, uneven layers with bubbles
Polish on the cuticles and side walls
Clean lines, even coverage and no smudges
Designs that are different on every nail by mistake

questions.stem: What usually causes air bubbles in nail polish?
options: Shaking the bottle hard, or applying thick coats
Using a thin base coat before the colour coat
Rolling the bottle gently between the palms
Letting each thin coat dry fully before adding the next one

questions.stem: How should ordinary nail polish with nail art on it be removed?
options: Scrape it off with a metal pusher while it is dry
Soak the hands in hot soapy water for half an hour
Peel it off with the fingernails of the other hand
Hold a pad soaked in remover on the nail, then wipe it off

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice helps nail art last longer?
options: Use the nails to open cans and scratch off labels
Wear gloves for housework and add top coat often
Soak the hands in hot water each day to soften the polish
Pick at any lifting edges to tidy them up

questions.stem: Why should a client not peel off gel polish herself?
options: It makes the gel turn a darker colour
It can strip layers off the natural nail and weaken it
It will mean she loses the art design for her next appointment
It is against the law to remove your own polish

questions.stem: Why should you check the time needed for a nail art design before you start?
options: So that you can take as long as you like over each nail
So that you can stop halfway and send her home
So the service fits the booking and the price agreed
So that the polish can be left open to dry out

questions.stem: A client wants a full set of hand-painted art. How should you tell her the price?
options: Tell her the full price in J$ before you start
Tell her the price only after the work is done
Charge whatever the client in front of her paid
Let her guess the price and pay what she likes

questions.stem: Which set-up is best for detailed nail art work?
options: A low stool with the client's hand on her lap
A dim, quiet room so that the client can relax and sleep
A busy reception desk near the door
Good bright light, a stable table and a hand rest

questions.stem: You want to photograph a client's finished nail art for the salon's portfolio. What must you do first?
options: Post it online at once while the polish is fresh
Take a photo of her face with the nails beside it
Ask her permission, and photograph only her hands
Ask the receptionist to sign the photo before you take it

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

essays.stem: Describe the consultation you would carry out before a nail art service.
essays.modelAnswer: I greet the client and look at her hands and nails in good light. I ask what the nail art is for, such as a wedding, a graduation, a holiday or everyday wear, and what colours and style she likes. I ask about her job and daily life, because some jobs, such as nursing or food handling, limit nail length or decoration, and heavy housework can damage gems and 3D art. I show her my portfolio, sample tips or a colour chart to help her choose, and suggest designs that suit her nail length and shape. I check her nails and skin for contraindications, and ask about allergies to nail products. We agree the design, the products (polish or gel), how long it will take and the price in J$ before I start. I write everything on the record card, including any nail conditions, and she signs it.
markingPoints: Asks about the occasion, colours and style wanted
Asks about her job and lifestyle and why it matters
Shows a portfolio or samples and suggests designs to suit her nails
Checks for contraindications and allergies
Agrees design, time and price; records it and the client signs

essays.stem: Explain which nail and skin conditions would stop or restrict a nail art service, and what you would do if you found one.
essays.modelAnswer: Some conditions stop the service, because they are infectious or could get worse. These include a fungal infection of the nail (the nail may be thick, yellow or crumbly), a bacterial infection around the nail with redness, swelling, heat or pus, warts around the nails, and broken or bleeding skin. If I find one of these, I do not work on the nail. I explain kindly, without naming an illness, that the nail needs to be checked, and I advise her to see a doctor or pharmacist. Other conditions restrict the service. A nail that is lifting from the nail bed, a bruised nail, a split or a very weak nail can be left out or treated gently, with no heavy decoration. A small cut can be avoided. A client with a known allergy to a product, such as gel, should have a different product. White spots and ridges are not contraindications. I record what I found on the record card.
markingPoints: Names conditions that stop the service (fungal or bacterial infection, warts, broken skin)
Does not treat, explains tactfully and refers to a doctor or pharmacist
Names conditions that restrict the service (lifting, bruised, split or weak nail, cut)
Adapts the products for allergies
Records the condition on the record card

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare a client's natural nails before applying nail art.
essays.modelAnswer: I wash my hands and ask the client to wash hers, or I clean her hands with an antibacterial product. I remove any old polish with cotton and remover, pressing on the nail for a moment and then wiping from the base to the tip. I check the nails and skin again for contraindications. I shape each nail to the agreed shape with a fine file, filing from the side to the centre in one direction so the nail does not split. I push the cuticles back gently and remove only loose dead skin. I buff the surface lightly if needed to remove shine. Then I wipe each nail with a nail cleanser (dehydrator) to remove oil and dust, so that the polish sticks well. I take care not to touch the nail plates with my fingers after this. Last, I apply a thin base coat to each nail, capping the free edge, and let it dry before the colour.
markingPoints: Hands cleaned and old polish removed correctly
Nails shaped with a fine file, filing in one direction
Cuticles pushed back gently
Nail plates cleansed of oil and dust before the base coat
Thin base coat applied and capped at the free edge

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan a balanced nail art design. Use the colour wheel and give an example for a Jamaican occasion.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the client's wishes, the occasion, her outfit and her nail length and shape. Short nails suit small, simple designs, and long nails have room for more detail. I choose a colour scheme using the colour wheel. Complementary colours, which sit opposite each other, such as purple and yellow, give strong contrast. Colours next to each other, such as green and blue, look calm and blended. I choose one focal point, often an accent nail on the ring finger, and keep the other nails simpler so the design is not too busy. I repeat colours or shapes across all ten nails so both hands look balanced. For example, for Independence Day I could paint a black base on most nails, add a gold diagonal stripe with striping tape, and paint the Jamaican flag's black, green and gold on the accent nails, sealed with top coat. I sketch the plan on paper or a practice tip first.
markingPoints: Considers the client's wishes, occasion and nail length and shape
Uses the colour wheel correctly (complementary and neighbouring colours)
Uses a focal point or accent nail and avoids crowding
Keeps both hands balanced by repeating colours or shapes
Gives a suitable Jamaican example and plans it on paper or a tip first

essays.stem: Describe the main freehand nail art tools and techniques, and how you would keep your work neat.
essays.modelAnswer: A striper brush has long, thin bristles. It holds enough paint to make long, fine, straight lines in one smooth stroke. A detail brush is short and fine, for small shapes such as flowers, leaves and outlines. A fan brush gives soft streaks and feathered effects. A dotting tool has a small ball on the end; it makes neat dots, and larger or smaller balls give different sizes. A sponge dabs on colours to make an ombre. To keep work neat, I rest my hand and the client's hand on a stable surface or hand rest, and work in good light. I use nail art paint or polish of the right thickness and take only a little on the brush. I let each layer dry before the next so colours do not drag. I clean my brushes often, with water for water-based paints and remover for polish. I clean any paint off the skin with a fine brush dipped in remover, and seal the finished art with top coat.
markingPoints: Striper brush for long fine lines; detail brush for small shapes
Fan brush for streaks; dotting tool for dots; sponge for ombre
Steady hands supported on a stable surface, with good light
Small amounts of product, each layer dried, brushes cleaned in the right solvent
Cleans mistakes off the skin and seals the art with top coat

essays.stem: Describe how you would apply gems, transfer foil and decals so that they look neat and last.
essays.modelAnswer: For gems, I paint the colour and let it dry. I place a small dot of top coat, gel or nail adhesive where each gem will sit. I pick the gem up with a wax pencil or a slightly damp dotting tool and press it gently into place, then seal around it with top coat, or cure it if I am using gel, so it does not catch on clothes or hair. For transfer foil, I brush on foil adhesive and wait until it turns clear and tacky. I press the foil on, shiny side up, rub it smooth with an orange stick or my finger, then peel it off quickly, leaving the pattern behind. I seal it with top coat. For a sticker decal, I place it with tweezers and press it flat. A water-slide decal is soaked briefly, slid onto the nail and smoothed. Every decal is sealed with top coat, capping the free edge. I keep gems small on short nails and check that nothing has sharp edges.
markingPoints: Gems: set in top coat, gel or adhesive, placed with a wax pencil or dotting tool
Gems sealed or cured so they do not catch
Foil: adhesive left to go clear and tacky, foil pressed on and peeled, then sealed
Decals placed flat with tweezers (water-slide soaked and slid) and sealed
Caps the free edge and checks for sharp edges

essays.stem: Explain how you would work safely with nail art products, including ventilation, fire safety, storage, PPE and first aid.
essays.modelAnswer: Nail polish, top coat, remover and gel products give off fumes and many are flammable, so I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. I work in a well-ventilated area, keep the lids on bottles when they are not in use, and use only small amounts. I keep products away from heat, sparks and flames, and nobody smokes near the nail station. I store products tightly closed, in their labelled containers, in a cool, dark place, away from food and out of reach of children. I read the safety data sheet to know the hazards, safe use and first aid for each product. I wear gloves when using solvents and a dust mask when filing, and I keep uncured gel off the skin, because it can cause an allergy. Cotton soaked in remover goes in a lidded metal bin that is emptied often. If a product splashes into an eye, I rinse it at once with plenty of clean cool water and get medical help if it stays sore.
markingPoints: Good ventilation and lids kept on
Products kept away from heat and flames (flammable); no smoking
Correct storage: closed, labelled, cool and dark, away from food
PPE: gloves and dust mask; uncured gel kept off the skin; safety data sheets read
Correct waste disposal and first aid for a splash in the eye

essays.stem: Describe how you would keep the nail station, tools and brushes hygienic for every client.
essays.modelAnswer: Before each client I wash my hands, wipe the station with a salon disinfectant and lay down a clean towel. I ask the client to wash her hands, or clean them with an antibacterial product. Single-use items, such as orange sticks, cotton, wipes, and files and buffers that cannot be disinfected, are used for one client only and then thrown away in a lined, lidded bin. Metal tools, such as dotting tools, nippers and pushers, are cleaned with soap and water to remove product and dust, then disinfected for the full time the maker gives, or sterilised. I store clean tools in a clean, covered container. A UV cabinet is only for storing tools that are already clean and disinfected. Art brushes are wiped clean straight after use with the right cleaner, such as water for water-based paints, remover for polish or gel cleanser for gel, and stored with the bristles covered and, for gel brushes, away from light. I never treat infected nails, and I keep food and drinks away from the station.
markingPoints: Hand washing and a disinfected station with a clean towel
Single-use items used once and thrown away
Metal tools cleaned then disinfected or sterilised, and stored clean
Knows a UV cabinet only stores clean tools
Brushes cleaned with the right cleaner and stored correctly

essays.stem: Explain how gel polish is used for nail art, and how gel nail art should be removed safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Gel polish stays soft until it is cured, or hardened, under an LED or UV lamp. After preparing the nails, I apply a thin gel base coat, keeping it off the skin and cuticles, and cure it for the time the gel maker gives. I apply thin coats of colour and cure each one. I can then paint designs with gel art paints, place gems in gel, or add foils, curing each layer. If a layer touches the skin, I clean it off with a brush before curing, because uncured gel on the skin can cause an allergy. I finish with a gel top coat, capping the free edge, cure it, and wipe off any sticky layer with the cleanser the maker gives. To remove gel, I never peel it off. I lightly file the shiny top layer, soak the nails in remover with cotton and foil wraps, or as the maker says, then gently push the softened gel off with an orange stick. I finish with cuticle oil.
markingPoints: Gel cures under an LED or UV lamp for the time the maker gives
Thin coats, each cured; art added and cured in layers
Gel kept off the skin, with the reason
Top coat capped, cured and sticky layer wiped off
Safe removal: no peeling, file the top, soak off, push gently, oil

essays.stem: Describe how you would check the quality of finished nail art, and the aftercare advice you would give the client.
essays.modelAnswer: I check every nail in good light. The base colour should be smooth and even, with no streaks, bubbles or thin patches. Lines should be clean and straight, dots even in size, and the design should match the plan and be balanced across both hands. There should be no polish on the cuticles or side walls, and any gems should be secure, with no sharp edges. The top coat must cover all the art and be capped over the free edge. I show the client and check that she is happy. For aftercare, she should wear gloves for housework and washing, avoid using her nails as tools, and add a thin top coat every few days to protect the art. She should use cuticle oil daily. She should not pick or peel the art, and for gel she should come back to the salon for safe removal, usually in about two to three weeks. I write the design and products on her record card and suggest a date to return.
markingPoints: Checks the colour is smooth and even, with no bubbles or streaks
Checks lines, dots, balance, clean cuticles and secure gems
Checks the top coat seals the art and caps the free edge; client is happy
Aftercare: gloves, no using nails as tools, top coat, cuticle oil
No picking; return for gel removal; records and rebooks

practical1.title: Nail art display on practice tips: a themed design board
practical1.brief: As a group, choose one theme with the assessor, for example Independence Day, Christmas, carnival, or a beach wedding in Negril. Each member plans five different designs for the theme on a design sheet, then paints them on five practice nail tips, using at least five different techniques between them: dots, stripes with a striper brush or striping tape, an ombre with a sponge, a French tip, marbling, stamping, a decal or foil, and gems. Every tip has a base coat, colour, the art and a top coat. The group then mounts all the tips neatly on one display board with a title and each member's name under her tips. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up the stations, keeping the ventilation and waste safe, taking the photos, or mounting and labelling the board. Photograph each stage below. Hand in once for the whole group, with the design sheets.
materials: Practice nail tips and tip holders or sticks
Base coat, top coat, nail polishes and nail art paints in a range of colours
Striper, detail and fan brushes, dotting tools and small sponges
Striping tape, stamping plate, scraper and stamper
Decals, transfer foil and foil adhesive, gems and a wax pencil
Nail polish remover, a clean-up brush, cotton and orange sticks
Design sheets, a display board and labels
A lidded metal bin, salon disinfectant and paper towels
photos: Each member's design sheet for her five tips
The stations set up, with good light and ventilation
Tips with base coat and colour applied
A technique in progress on a tip (for example dotting, striping or sponging)
Each member's five finished, sealed tips
The finished display board with its title and names
The stations cleaned and the waste in the lidded bin
checklist: Planned five designs on the design sheet that suit the theme
Prepared each tip with a thin base coat
Used at least five different techniques correctly between the tips
Lines clean, dots even and colours applied smoothly with no bubbles
Gems, foils and decals secure, flat and sealed
Sealed every design with top coat, capping the free edge
Cleaned brushes and tools in the right cleaner
Worked safely with good ventilation and left the station clean
safety: Keep the area well ventilated and keep bottle lids on when not in use
Keep polishes, removers and adhesives away from heat and flames
Put cotton soaked in remover in a lidded metal bin
Wear gloves when using removers and solvents, and do not eat or drink at the station
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for every product

practical2.title: Nail art on a client's natural nails for an occasion
practical2.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as nail technician and client. In a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed to take part. The assessor gives each member an occasion, for example a graduation, a church harvest, a birthday party or a beach holiday. Each member holds a consultation, checks the client's nails and skin for contraindications, agrees a design, the time and a price in J$, and completes the record card. She prepares the natural nails, applies base coat and colour, and creates a design on all ten nails using at least two techniques, with one accent nail on each hand. She seals the art with top coat, checks the quality, and gives aftercare advice. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up the stations, checking ventilation and waste, taking the photos, or cleaning and disinfecting the tools at the end. Photograph each stage below. Photos show the hands and nails only. Hand in once for the whole group, with the record cards.
materials: Manicure stations with good light, hand rests and clean towels
Antibacterial hand product, nail polish remover, cotton and nail cleanser
Files, buffers, orange sticks and cuticle pushers
Base coat, top coat, polishes and nail art paints
Nail art brushes, dotting tools, sponges, striping tape, decals and gems
Clean-up brush and a portfolio or sample tips
Record cards and a price list in J$
Salon disinfectant, a lined, lidded bin and a lidded metal bin for solvent waste
photos: The client's nails before the service
The nails prepared and shaped, with base coat on
Colour applied to all ten nails
A technique in progress on the accent nail
The finished, sealed design on both hands
The station cleaned and tools in disinfectant
checklist: Held a consultation, checked for contraindications and agreed design, time and price
Prepared and shaped the nails correctly and cleansed the nail plates
Applied base coat and colour smoothly and evenly, capping the free edge
Used at least two techniques correctly, with a balanced design and accent nails
Kept the cuticles and side walls clean of product
Sealed the design with top coat and checked the quality
Gave correct aftercare advice and completed the record card
Worked hygienically and safely, and cleaned and disinfected the tools
safety: Do not work on nails with an infection, or on broken or bleeding skin: tell the assessor
Keep the area ventilated and the bottle lids closed when not in use
Keep products away from the client's eyes; if any gets in, rinse with plenty of clean cool water
Use single-use items once only and disinfect metal tools after use
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for every product
